notes: §1985:VIII.4.9.4 GR12: in extend mode 'The first record released ... has a relative record number one greater than the highest relative record number existing in the file', later ones consecutively higher, each moved into the RELATIVE KEY per MOVE. RelativeConnector#Write takes the sequential release for an EXTEND-open sequential connector; NextSequentialSlot answers max(highest existing key, last released) + 1, which for an unshared 1985 file is exactly highest + 1 then consecutive, and KeyedIoEmitter#EmitWrite moves the number into the key on success. Probes at 85: EXTEND on an empty file releases 1 (key preset 5 overwritten); after a random WRITE of record 8, EXTEND releases 9, and the next (10) with a PIC 9 key is invalid key 24 per GR14 c; OPEN EXTEND of a missing file answers 35 and the WRITE after it 48; a keyless EXTEND writes 00; OPEN EXTEND on a random file is refused (COBOL2372). The witness checks numbering past a hole and after DELETE of the top records.

next.reason: 1985 GR12, extend mode: the first record gets one more than the highest existing number, 'Subsequent records ... have consecutively higher relative record numbers', the number moved to the relative key. §2023:14.9.51.4 GR30 repeats this ('Subsequent records released to the operating environment have consecutively higher relative record numbers'), but §2023:14.9.51.4 GR29 adds 'If the physical file is shared and the open mode is extend, the record numbers are not necessarily consecutive' and §2023:14.9.51.4 GR31 'the relative key values returned are ascending, but not necessarily consecutive'. A 1985 program states no sharing, yet 2023 lets the implementor choose its sharing mode ('the implementor defines the sharing mode in which the file is opened', §2023:9.1.15), so its extend-mode numbers may skip where 1985 required consecutive ones. Looser.
